summary: Round 8 shows real, physically verified progress. Three-way parity at 2db27a7 is bit-exact with empty porcelain on all nodes. GitHub run 38856490617 concluded success on all three jobs, including Windows lock gating (66 passed) and hermetic CI (177 + 67 tests, 0 skipped). The production dry-run now agrees with the runtime guard (EN SKIP EXHAUSTED_TODAY, matching EN_2026-10-16.json). The increment still cannot be approved, for four reasons. (1) The mandated Rule 127 S05 live call exits 1, and this round's evidence contains no substitute proof. (2) The B3 resolution gate reports exit 0 while its own stdout says 'No module named scripts.orchestrator.run_pipeline', because the pipe into head masks the failure. (3) app/services/hhtech_reasoner.py references an undefined name `ancient_terms` in detect_safety_and_theme, which is a probable runtime NameError on the B1 viability path, and non-blocking ruff on app/ lets it through. (4) No post-HEAD scheduled cron tick is evidenced. The only post-HEAD production run (EN, 05:33 UTC, pid 152506) is off-schedule, has no stated provenance, and dispatched a real Telegram alert. In addition: the trend_engine_b1 diff is still truncated (Round 6 and 7 item), test isolation does not cover episodes or pending_tasks, the evidence harness still injects literal success narratives, scope remains bundled across AVF-VOX-001 and governance work, and source modules are gitignored under app/services.

component_reviews.analysis: In detect_safety_and_theme, `elif any(t in text for t in ancient_terms):` references `ancient_terms`. The diff defines truecrime/fraud/gambling/societal/history/tech term lists but no ancient_terms. Any subject that falls through the first five branches raises NameError. Both reason_topic_niche and assess_keyword_video_viability call this function outside their try blocks, so a NameError would crash the B1 candidate loop rather than produce a REJECTED_API_ERROR. CI runs `ruff check app/ --exit-zero` and Makefile ruff targets exclude this file, so F821 cannot block. The whole-file churn (1169 lines) persists despite .gitattributes, so the semantic change set (tech_terms branch, \bwar\b regex, '동탄문구점' removal) is still not isolated.

O_EXCL/link acquisition, the takeover mutex with re-check, the CORRUPT_FAIL_CLOSED seal, and pure-read is_market_done_today are sound and well tested. Remaining issues: (a) when the caller passes neither lock_token nor owner_pid, mark_completed and mark_exhausted_today verify against no expectations, so any caller can overwrite a held lock. test_b1_daily_guard_integration does exactly this. This contradicts the Round 4 mandate 'never overwrite a lock the caller does not own'. (b) The registry check treats B2-rejected EN_TEMP_* entries written by record_handled_topic as 'registry_committed_pending_render', which mislabels a rejection as a commit. (c) Production EN_2026-10-15.json now carries lock_token='legacy_migrated_token'. A production lock file was mutated, and no user confirmation or script provenance is shown (Rule 118 and Rule 137, Round 1 Item 10).

Atomic single-lock reservation, delta-safe rollback, and Windows is_pid_alive semantics are correct and pass on windows-latest. Residual race: on tombstone content mismatch, `os.replace(tombstone, lock_file)` can clobber a lock that a third contender created via O_EXCL after the rename. Use os.link(tombstone, lock_file) (fails if it exists) and then unlink the tombstone. _read_cooldown_data catches all exceptions, including transient OSError on open, and quarantines a possibly valid state file. Restrict quarantine to JSONDecodeError and ValueError.
